istanbul_ambarli_centre_about.title: About the Centre
istanbul_ambarli_centre_about.note: There's no physical seafarers' club at Ambarlı. Stella Maris / Apostleship of the Sea operates purely as a ship-visiting mission here — a chaplain comes to you, arranged in advance through your ship's agent, rather than you going to a centre.

istanbul_ambarli_transport_taxi.title: Taxi

rows.title: Order strictly to the main Altaş Gate
rows.sub: City taxis are not allowed inside the berth areas

istanbul_ambarli_transport_taxi.note: Licensed Istanbul taxis are yellow (or blue/black), marked "TAKŞİ", with a working taksimetre (meter) visible on the rear-view mirror. Drivers offering a fixed "no meter" price right at the checkpoint booth are private operators — avoid them. Always check the meter is actually running; some "forget" to start it, especially in tourist areas. No pre-payment needed.

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you. In some countries this is a criminal offence — and it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: Being asked to go somewhere private
rows.sub: A car, a back room, an alley — a legitimate exchange never needs this

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Know the rough official rate first
rows.sub: Check on your phone before you go — so you can spot a bad deal immediately

rows.title: Count what you receive, before you walk away
rows.sub: In front of the person who gave it to you, not after
